title: honeycomb: move wk wrapper behaviour into the engine (simplify; focus follows humans, never agents)
description:
Move worktree lifecycle behaviour out of the Nushell `wk` wrapper (`lib/honeycomb/nu/honeycomb/`, ~475 lines) into the honeycomb engine, leaving the shell layer as a thin alias whose only irreducible job is changing the calling shell's cwd.

This is a simplification. `wk` works well today; the goal is to move the same behaviour into TypeScript and delete duplication, not to add new safety machinery.

## What moves

- Post-create setup and its rollback (today: wrapper runs the script, then rolls back via the `HONEYCOMB_INTERNAL_ROLLBACK` backdoor and a raw `git branch -f`).
- tmux open/switch/close and session naming (already emitted as `session.name`).
- The fzf worktree picker.
- `--self` resolution and human status lines.

The pool-full recycle picker already exists in the engine (`pickFullPoolSlot`); the wrapper only reimplemented it because it calls `--json`. The shim will call human mode, so it disappears for free.

## Focus follows the human, never the agent

One flag, `--interactive`, passed only by `wk`:

- **With it**: `add` opens and focuses the worktree's multiplexer session (or tells the shell to `cd` when not in a multiplexer); `remove`/`finish` close sessions for removed worktrees and send the shell to the canonical root if it was inside one.
- **Without it** (agents, scripts): no multiplexer calls and no cd directive at all. An agent can't steal focus or kill a session because it never touches sessions.

Terminal detection is deliberately not used: agents run inside the user's tmux panes and can have a PTY.

## Decisions

- `add` always runs setup in the engine. No deferred mode. `post_create_script_path` stays in JSON as always `null`.
- Multiplexer support is a small injected service (tmux first) so another multiplexer with a similar API could replace it.
- Shell cwd handoff: the engine writes a directory path to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`.
- `remove --self` is a boolean (the worktree containing `--cwd`).
- JSON changes are additive only.

## End state

`mod.nu` is a ~30-line shim; `tmux.nu` is deleted.

title: honeycomb: HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE shell cwd handoff
description:
Implement the `HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE` directive exactly as specified in the spec task.

## Scope

- Add a directive-file operation behind an injected service (`WorkspaceFiles` has none today, `src/services.ts`).
- Write only when interactive, on success, and when focus did not move via the multiplexer (including when multiplexer focus failed):
  - `add --open` → worktree path;
  - removal of the worktree containing the caller's shell cwd → the canonical root.
- Atomic write (temp + rename), absolute existing path, UTF-8 with trailing newline; never write partial or stale content.
- No internal `chdir` needed for git (`LiveGitRunner` already runs from `/`, `src/git/executor.ts`); verify removal works when the engine's own process cwd is inside the removed worktree.

## Acceptance

- Tests for each write/omit case, including multiplexer-focus failure → file written, and non-interactive → never written.

title: honeycomb: pick command replacing the wrapper's worktree picker
description:
Add `honeycomb pick`, replacing `pick-worktree` in `mod.nu`, so `wk switch` / `wk select` become one-line aliases.

## Scope

- fzf over `list` results (current worktree marked, as today). Preview via `multiplexer.previewCommand()`. Popup inside tmux, inline otherwise (check whether current fzf's `--tmux` replaces `fzf-tmux`).
- `--open`: `multiplexer.open(...)` the selection. Otherwise write it to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE` and print the path.
- Fix `src/fzf.ts` to check fzf's exit status, so cancel (1/130) exits cleanly and real failures error. Its `tty` option is currently a no-op; remove or implement it.

## Acceptance

- Tests with a fake picker: select, `--open`, cancel.

title: honeycomb: reduce wk Nushell wrapper to a thin shim
description:
Reduce the Nushell wrapper to a thin shim.

## Scope

- Rewrite `lib/honeycomb/nu/honeycomb/mod.nu`: one `def --env` helper that creates a temp cd file, runs `honeycomb --interactive …` with `HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE` without capturing stdio, propagates the exit code, `cd`s if the file has a path, and deletes it.
  - `wk add` → `add --branch … [--base …|--base-current] [--force]`
  - `wk remove` → `remove [--branch …|--self] [--force]`
  - `wk finish`, `wk copy`, `wk list`, `wk root`, `wk path` → pass-throughs
  - `wk switch` → `pick --open`; `wk select` → `pick`
- Delete `tmux.nu` and the remaining helpers. Trim `nu/honeycomb/tests/nushell.test.ts` to a smoke test of the cd handoff and exit code.
- Update the README "Nushell wrapper" section and `lib/honeycomb/AGENTS.md`.

## Acceptance

- `mod.nu` has no JSON parsing, git, tmux or prompts.
- Manual check in tmux: `wk add x` switches to the new session; `honeycomb add --branch y` from another pane (as an agent would) leaves your client alone.
- `bun run check` and honeycomb tests pass.

title: honeycomb: explicit --interactive authorisation, decoupled from --json
description:
Introduce explicit interaction authorisation in the engine and decouple prompting from output format.

Today `--json` means both "machine output" and "never prompt", which is why the wrapper reimplements the pool-full picker. After this task `--json` controls only stdout format and `--interactive` controls prompting/focus.

## Scope

- Global `--interactive` / `--no-interactive`; default non-interactive. No TTY or `$TMUX` inference.
- Restructure resolution: `main` builds `Deps` via `createLiveDeps()` before Commander parses (`src/cli.ts:12`, `:379`), and `optsToArgs` drops `false` values (`src/cli.ts`) so negated flags are lost. Resolve the mode after parsing and inject it (e.g. `Deps.interaction` or a per-dispatch context); keep tests able to supply it directly.
- `add` pool-full path: interactive → existing `pickFullPoolSlot` + `confirm` regardless of `--json`, then the normal `ready` payload; non-interactive → `pool_full` as today (exit `BLOCKED`). `--force` still skips confirmation.
- Picker/confirm must talk to `/dev/tty` so they work while stdout is captured (confirm does; the fzf helper's `tty` option is currently a no-op — fix or route through `/dev/tty`).

## Acceptance

- `add --json --interactive` on a full pool prompts and returns `kind: "ready"`; `add --json` returns `pool_full` unchanged even under a PTY.
- Unit tests use a fake `PickerService`; no test depends on a real TTY.

title: honeycomb: stderr messages under --json, human summaries, payload shape test

Make engine output sufficient for thin callers, and lock in JSON stability.

## Scope

- Under `--json`, `blocked`/failure payloads also write their `message` to stderr, so a shim needs only the exit code.
- Non-JSON mode prints a one-line human summary on stderr for `add`, `remove`, `finish`, `copy` (replacing the wrapper's "wk: …" lines). Paths callers need stay on stdout or in the payload.
- Add a payload shape regression test (per `kind`, per command) asserting all existing fields remain present, so later tasks can only add fields.
- Introduce the shared type(s) for additive structured results used by later tasks (session results, setup/rollback results) if doing so here keeps later diffs smaller; otherwise leave to those tasks.

## Acceptance

- Existing `kind` values and fields unchanged; shape test in place.

title: honeycomb: complete, observable rollback boundary for add/allocation
description:
Harden the add/allocation transaction so engine-run setup (next task) has a complete, observable rollback boundary.

## Scope

- The transaction starts at checkout creation / slot allocation and covers everything after it. Today script writing (if the next task keeps a script file) and the pooled missing-command check sit outside the rollback regions (`src/commands/add.ts` ~128–150, ~377–400, ~483–500).
- Rollback (`rollbackNonPoolAdd`, `rollbackPooledAllocation`) uses `runRaw` and ignores failures. Make each compensation step report success/failure and return a structured rollback result; preserve both the original error and any rollback errors.
- Expose failure as a structured payload (e.g. `blocked` with `reason: "setup_failed"` plus a `rollback` object) with non-zero exit, without changing existing kinds' fields.
- No change yet to who runs the script.

## Acceptance

- Tests with fake git/files: failure at copy, script write, missing pooled command → worktree removed/slot freed, new branch deleted, pre-existing branch head restored; injected rollback failure → both errors reported.

title: honeycomb: add always runs setup in the engine; delete wrapper rollback backdoor
description:

## Scope

- Run it the same way pool initialisation does (`src/application/pool.ts`, `HookRunner`). Drop the temp script file if running the command directly with `WK_ROOT`/`WK_CREATED` in the env is equivalent.
- Under `--json`, setup output goes to stderr so stdout stays a single JSON document.
- Keep `post_create_script_path` in the payload, always `null`.
- The wrapper's `run-post-create` and `rollback-add-payload` become dead code (they no-op on a null path): delete them, plus `HONEYCOMB_INTERNAL_ROLLBACK`, `Deps.internalRollback`, `remove --skip-pre-remote-check` and its handling in `src/protocol.ts` / `src/commands/remove.ts`.

title: honeycomb: multiplexer service with tmux implementation

title: honeycomb: --interactive flag drives session open/close and cd directive
description:
Add the `--interactive` flag and wire the multiplexer and cd directive into `add`, `remove` and `finish`.

## Scope

- Global `--interactive` option, read after Commander parses and passed through `Deps` or dispatch.
- With `--interactive`:
  - `add`: `multiplexer.open(...)` for the new worktree; outside a multiplexer, write the worktree path to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`.
  - `remove` / `finish` cleanup: if the shell's cwd was inside the removed worktree, write the canonical root to `$HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE`; then `multiplexer.closeUnder(path)` as the **last** step, after output is written (closing the invoking session may kill this process).
- Without `--interactive`: no multiplexer calls, no cd file.
- tmux failures are a warning on stderr; they never undo the git operation.
- Git already runs from `/` (`src/git/executor.ts`), so removing the worktree containing the process cwd needs no extra handling. Verify.

## Acceptance

- Fake-multiplexer tests: interactive add opens; non-interactive add/remove make no multiplexer calls; interactive remove writes the canonical root and closes sessions last.
notes:
Remove the matching item from the spec's pending-changes list (lib/honeycomb/devflow/specs/git-worktrees.md) when this lands.
Implemented on branch hv-honeycomb-engine-owns-wk-2by.9 (commit 2640803, worktree .worktrees/hv-honeycomb-engine-owns-wk-2by.9; not merged). Branched from hv-honeycomb-engine-owns-wk-2by.7 (multiplexer, closed but unmerged); 2by.4 and 2by.6 are also unmerged and touch add/remove, so expect conflicts when integrating (add.ts post-create/projectName lines in particular). Design: --interactive is a Commander global passed through args like --cwd (parseOptions boolean; finish allows it). Multiplexer gains readonly attached (tmux true, NoMultiplexer false). Deps gains cdDirective (FileCdDirective writes the path to $HONEYCOMB_CD_FILE, no-op when unset).
